title: The Last Exception for Two-Colour Rado Numbers of x + y + c = kz
description: Unconditional pure core Lean 4 formalization (zero external dependencies, zero Mathlib imports, zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms only) determining the exact last exception c*(k) for the 2-colour Rado number R(c, k) of x + y + c = kz for every integer k >= 3, where c*(k) = k(k^2 + k - 4)/2 for odd k and k(k^2 - 2)/2 for even k. Both halves are formalized unconditionally: (1) an original reflection proof (x |-> N+1-x) of the upper half R(c, k) = LB(c, k) for every valid c > c*(k) (valid means k odd or c even), and (2) Martinelli and Schaal's (2007) Lemma 3 lower half showing non-forcing at LB(c*(k), k), i.e., there exists a 2-colouring of [1, LB(c*(k), k)] with no monochromatic solution of x + y + c*(k) = k z (so ¬ Forced (c*(k)) k (LB (c*(k)) k) and c*(k) is an exception to R(c, k) = LB(c, k); finite existence of R(c*(k), k) itself is not formalized). In nu_iff, the property "R(c, k) = LB(c, k) for all valid c >= v" holds iff c*(k) < v, so the least integer cutoff is c*(k) + 1 while the least valid cutoff nu(k) (requiring Valid nu(k) k, i.e., even when k is even) is c*(k) + 1 for odd k and c*(k) + 2 for even k, giving least valid cutoffs 13, 30, 66, 104, 183, 250, 388, 492 for k = 3..10 and settling the Kim-Song-Hwang (2023) conjecture nu(5) = 66.
